summary:
Governance lens, source-only review of the packet at commit 1dc5ed1; nothing was executed and every finding is an inference from the numbered source.

The structural guardrails are real in code: agents change state only through proposals, the server refuses threat catalogs, disabled frameworks and out-of-scope levels for people and agents alike, licensed AICPA text is gated before it reaches the model, and threat links stay out of the crosswalk.

The weak layer is evidence and the claims built on it. Five findings are launch blockers for a product whose promise is "Prove every claim":

1. **Accepted evidence is mutable.** A contributor can extend the validity or relink accepted evidence without re-review, and an unparseable date never expires.
2. **Agent-written text becomes accepted evidence.** Approving the proposal (or granted autonomy) files it as accepted, with no artifact, no hash and no restriction on kind.
3. **Superseded evidence turns requirements at-risk.** Any expired item flags the requirement even when a newer valid one exists, and each person-run connector files a new 30-day item.
4. **Connector runs self-accept weak evidence.** A contributor's run files presence heuristics (for example a CODEOWNERS file) as accepted evidence for broad requirements.
5. **Crosswalk projections can propose "Implemented" from weak mappings.** The mapping strength cancels out of the mean, and no server rule ties agent-proposed levels to evidence.

A sixth is conditional: if the installation is multi-tenant and holds an AICPA copy, that text is served to every signed-in tenant.

The remaining findings are fidelity gaps: unverified citations, trust-center figures, OSCAL status tokens, positional obligation ids, audit-chain coverage and a wrong policy-template fallback.

Recommended next phase: Evidence foundations, delivered as one workflow (collect → review → supersede → claim → export with lineage). Then one API-depth connector, then the auditor workspace. Framework expansion and SAML/SCIM are growth work and should follow, because each new framework or identity feature multiplies claims resting on the current evidence model.
coverage: Agents: definitions and tool subsets (agents.ts), Claude tool loop (claude.ts), host contract, runtime context, all eight offline playbooks, the policy composer
Tool permissions and proposal validation: tools.ts refusals, VisuaService.checkProposal / createProposal / decideProposal / applyProposal, autonomy, approval edits
Licensed-text boundary: mode.ts, modelText / modelTask / passageAllowed, licensing tests, corpus file / framework graph / search routes, .local handling, NOTICE.md and corpus/README.md
Corpus ingestion, search and citations: CSF, SP 800-53, RMF, AI RMF, overlays, state laws, threats, TSC skeleton and mappings, pdf.ts, search.ts, scripts/ingest.ts, citation normalization
Framework scope, status and scoring: scopeOf, initializeStates, updateState, deriveStatus, scoreFramework, scoreOf (law timing), planner, recommend, tiers, FIPS 199
Threat mappings and coverage: threat-links.ts, threat-paths.ts, services/threats.ts (coverage, pooling, ring, Observatory bundle), threatBrief
Trust claims: public trust-center route, trust.ts, README / roadmap / architecture claims compared with code
Reports and exports: CSF profile, action plan, evidence index, AI RMF profile, SOC 2 PBC, readiness Markdown, OSCAL SSP and POA&M, SOC 2 DC 200 description
Connectors: web posture and repository hygiene, their requirement mappings, evidence filing for person and agent runs
Audit trail as it bears on claims: log, chainHash, verifyAuditTrail, actor recording for agent and autonomy paths
Access matrix (packages/core/access.ts) against route capability declarations in app.ts for evidence, policy, connector and proposal routes

findings.mechanism: Launch blocker. PATCH /evidence/:id without a `decision` needs only the write floor (no work.approve check) and passes title, requirementIds and validUntil to updateEvidence. That method spreads the changes over the stored record and keeps status 'accepted', reviewedBy and sha256. A contributor can therefore (a) push validUntil to any future date and (b) relink accepted evidence to any other requirements, without re-review. This includes connector-check evidence, whose 30-day window and requirement links are meant to come from the recorded check. Separately, validUntil is an unvalidated string on create and update: for an unparseable value `new Date(x).getTime()` is NaN, both comparisons are false, and the evidence is valid and 'fresh' forever. Trigger: as a contributor, PATCH an accepted item with {"validUntil":"2099-01-01","requirementIds":["nist-csf-2.0:PR.AA-01"]}, or with {"validUntil":"n/a"}.
findings.evidence: app.ts:522-527 gates only the decision branch with requireCapability('work.approve'); line 527 forwards requirementIds and validUntil. visua.ts:1064-1066 builds `{ ...prev, ...changes }` with no status reset. Schemas at app.ts:165 and :172 declare `validUntil: z.string().optional()`. status.ts:21 `new Date(e.validUntil).getTime() < now.getTime()` and :27-29 are NaN-unsafe. access.ts:18 reserves 'accept evidence' for work.approve.
findings.recommendation: Treat acceptance as binding on (content hash, requirement links, validity window). A change to links or validUntil on accepted evidence should either require work.approve or return the item to pending-review with the previous review kept in history. Make connector-sourced evidence immutable except by supersession. Validate validUntil / collectedAt as ISO dates in zod and treat unparseable stored values as expired. Add API tests for a contributor extending and relinking accepted evidence.

findings.mechanism: Launch blocker. A `create-evidence` proposal without a checkResultId is applied by creating evidence with `status: "accepted"`, `source: "agent"` and `content` equal to the text the model wrote. Approving the proposal is the only review, and with `autonomy["create-evidence"]` set (the settings schema accepts any key) the reviewer is the literal string "autonomy". No artifact is attached and no sha256 is computed; only uploads and checks are hashed. The kind is unrestricted, so an agent can file 'attestation' or 'automated-check' evidence. The offline Assessor counts any valid kind 'automated-check' item as a passing check (offline.ts:406, 413), which supports a level-3 proposal. The rule that agents never file plans or drafts as evidence lives only in the tool description and the role prompt. A second gap: approval `edits` are merged over the payload, so an approver who sends {"checkResultId":null,"content":"…"} moves a check-backed proposal onto the free-text path with edited content. That contradicts 'edits cannot change what the check observed'. Trigger: run evidence-collector or task-executor on Claude, let it call propose_evidence with a narrative, approve it (or enable autonomy); the requirement gains valid evidence and evidence coverage rises.
findings.evidence: visua.ts:1633-1645 creates accepted evidence with no sha256. visua.ts:1550 `if (ws.autonomy[proposal.type]) return this.decideProposal(…, "autonomy")`. tools.ts:580 kind enum includes attestation and automated-check; :575 holds the prohibition as description text only. visua.ts:1510-1516 checkProposal validates links only. visua.ts:1560 `payload: { ...prev.payload, ...(edits ?? {}) }` and :1628 branches on `typeof payload["checkResultId"] === "string"`. README:38 advertises evidence provenance with SHA-256. docs/architecture.md:248 says 'Evidence proposals are restricted'.
findings.recommendation: Server-side: (1) file agent-proposed evidence as pending-review, so proposal approval creates the record and a separate accept step (work.approve) accepts it; never auto-accept through autonomy unless it is check-backed. (2) Restrict agent kinds: no attestation, and 'automated-check' only with a checkResultId. (3) Hash content on every path. (4) Require a reference to an artifact (upload id, check id, connector observation) and mark narrative-only items as 'unsupported statement', excluded from isEvidenceValid. (5) Make checkResultId immutable under edits, or whitelist editable fields per proposal type.

findings.mechanism: Launch blocker. deriveStatus marks a requirement at-risk when any linked evidence item is expired and current > 0, without checking whether a newer valid item supersedes it. evidenceFreshness returns 'expired' from validUntil alone, so rejected or pending items with a past date also count. Nothing in the packet supersedes or retires old evidence. A person's connector run files a new 30-day evidence item for every passing check on every run; the 'already on file' de-duplication exists only in the agent tool. Trigger: run a connector on day 0 and again on day 31 with the check still passing. Each mapped requirement with current > 0 now has one expired and one fresh item and shows at-risk ('1 evidence item(s) expired') from then on. The same happens to requirements governed by a re-approved policy once the older version's evidence passes its review date. The automated-monitoring path therefore degrades into a standing false at-risk signal that only an approver's manual status override hides.
findings.evidence: status.ts:59-60 `const expired = evidence.filter((e) => evidenceFreshness(e, now) === "expired"); if (expired.length && current > 0) reasons.push(...)`, then :65 returns at-risk. status.ts:27-28 has no status check before returning 'expired'. visua.ts:1264 files evidence for every pass with no existing-evidence check; :1290 sets validUntil to observedAt + 30 days. tools.ts:689-696 `onFile` is applied only in run_checks. Inference: the storage layer is not in the packet, so a background expiry or cleanup job cannot be ruled out, but no service code sets status 'expired' or removes evidence.
findings.recommendation: Model supersession explicitly: evidence carries a series key (connectorId + checkId + requirement, or policyId), and a new accepted item marks the previous one superseded. The at-risk rule should fire only when a requirement at level > 0 has no valid evidence left in a series that previously had some. Ignore rejected and pending items. Apply the 'already on file' rule to person-run connectors, or refresh the existing item's observation instead of filing a new one. Add a core test: expired + fresh evidence of the same series must not yield at-risk.

findings.mechanism: Launch blocker for the evidence claim. The connector run route needs only the write floor, and a person's run files every passing check as `status: "accepted"` evidence reviewed by "system:connector", labeled `automation: "api-automated"`. A contributor thereby produces accepted evidence without the approver capability that accepting evidence otherwise needs; the same check run by an agent needs approval. The check-to-requirement mappings are hard-coded and Visua-authored. Several are presence heuristics filed against broad requirements: a CODEOWNERS file → CC8.1 / CM-3; a lockfile → SA-10 / CC8.1; 'no secret regex hit' in at most 4,000 files under 512 KB → CC6.1 / IA-5 / PR.AA-01; three of four browser headers → CC6.6 / CM-6. Each item counts toward evidence coverage and satisfies the evidence requirement for 'verified'. The offline Assessor also treats one passing check plus one done task as grounds to propose level 3. Trigger: as a contributor, POST /connectors/:id/run on a repository containing an empty CODEOWNERS file; CC8.1 gains accepted evidence.
findings.evidence: app.ts:555 has no need(). visua.ts:1264 files evidence as "system:connector"; :1286 `status: "accepted"`; :1292 `automation: "api-automated"`. repo-scan.ts:87, :98, :107, :116, :138 hold the mappings; :21-47 the scan limits. offline.ts:406-415 counts kind 'automated-check' as passing. README:104 and access.ts:18 assign 'accept evidence' to the approver. docs/roadmap.md:124 says integrations are labeled with their real automation depth, but repo-scan reads a local path and is not API automation.
findings.recommendation: File person-run check evidence as pending-review unless the workspace opts into auto-acceptance per check. Give each check an assurance scope (for example 'indicator of' versus 'demonstrates') and let only 'demonstrates' checks satisfy evidence coverage for their requirement. Label automation depth truthfully per connector. Move the mapping table into data carrying 'Visua editorial' as its authority, as the RMF mapping set already does.

findings.mechanism: Launch blocker for the invariant 'a mapping is never evidence'. In projectLevels, `mean = Σ(current × strength) / Σ(strength)` is a strength-weighted average of the source levels, so when all edges share one relationship the strength cancels. With every mapped source at level 4 over weak 'related-to' edges (0.35), best = 1.4 and mean = 4, so suggested = round(2.7) = 3. Confidence is 'medium' whenever there are two or more sources of any strength, and the Crosswalk Analyst proposes everything that is not 'low'. In the shipped sets every edge seen from a SOC 2 criterion or an SP 800-53 control is 'related-to': the inverse of 'supports' is 'related-to', and the composed and editorial sets are 'related-to' or 'supports'. Routine runs therefore propose 'Implemented' (RMF) or 'Operating — Type 2 ready' (SOC 2) from mapping alone, across scales with different meanings and not capped at target. The offline rationale names codes and relationships but not the mapping authority, which the role prompt requires, and carries no citations. The server gate checks only node, framework and scope; the Assessor's 'no level above 2 without accepted evidence' rule exists only in the prompt. With `autonomy["set-level"]` these apply unattended. Trigger: CSF outcomes at level 4, SOC 2 enabled with the local AICPA mappings, run crosswalk-analyst; proposals to raise criteria to level 3 at medium confidence.
findings.evidence: crosswalk.ts:125-134 computes best, weighted and suggested; :134 the confidence rule. crosswalk.ts:18 `supports: "related-to"` in INVERSE. tsc-mappings.ts:79 and :119 and csf.ts:231, :242 set the relationships. offline.ts:610 filters `p.confidence !== "low"`; :618-623 calls proposeAssessment with no citations and a rationale lacking authority. agents.ts:42 and :84 hold the prompt-only rules. visua.ts:1506-1507 is the server check.
findings.recommendation: Fix the math: suggested = round(max over sources of current × strength), capped at target, and derive confidence from the best strength, not the source count. Convert between family scales explicitly or refuse cross-scale projection above the lowest evidenced level. Enforce on the server, for agent-originated set-level proposals, that a level above 2 requires valid evidence on the target requirement itself (otherwise cap or reject), and that projections from editorial or composed sets are marked as such and never auto-applied. Include the mapping set authority and document in the rationale and citations.

findings.mechanism: normalizeCitations keeps any model-supplied citation whose documentId exists in a manifest and stores the model's own `quote`, `page` and `locator` unchecked. A Claude-run agent can attach an invented or paraphrased quote and page to a real document, and the approver sees it as a corpus citation. Citations with unknown ids are dropped silently and the proposal proceeds with none. Proposals for targets, applicability, tasks, evidence, task updates and check evidence always carry `citations: []`, and Crosswalk Analyst assessments pass none, so the README claim 'Every agent action is cited to the official framework text' is not supported by recorded facts. Offline, citeFor takes the top BM25 hits for code + title + text rather than the node's own pinned citation, so the attached page can belong to a different passage. Quotes are also not strictly verbatim: pdf.ts re-joins every line-end hyphen (including real compounds) and bestQuote truncates with an ellipsis.
findings.evidence: tools.ts:54-61 filters only on `host.registry.documents.has(c.documentId)` and copies `quote: c.quote.slice(0, 600)`. tools.ts:483, :505, :536, :593, :620, :702 pass `citations: []`. offline.ts:71 runs a search instead of using node.citation. pdf.ts:37 `.replace(/(\w)-\n(\w)/g, "$1$2")`. search.ts:140 truncates. agents.ts:114 states 'No citation, no claim'.
findings.recommendation: Have search_corpus return chunk ids and accept citations by chunk id, or verify that the whitespace-normalized quote occurs in a chunk of that document and page. Store `verified: true|false` and show unverified citations as such. Attach the requirement node's own citation automatically to every proposal that names a node. Reword the README claim to what is recorded: assessments and policies carry corpus citations; other proposals reference the requirement.

findings.mechanism: Conditional launch blocker (hosted multi-tenant installation holding an AICPA copy). The framework graph, node, search and corpus-file routes need only a signed-in principal and are not tenant-scoped. The servable() filter excludes `.local` folders, but the AICPA documents live in corpus/aicpa-soc2/ (git-ignored, not .local). Once the operator adds its licensed copy, every tenant can download the AICPA PDFs and workbooks and read the verbatim criteria, points of focus and search quotes. The licence note in corpus/README.md describes personal, non-commercial use for 'this installation', while the README positions v0.1 for multi-tenant hosting. Whether this breaches AICPA's terms is a licensing question for the operator and is not assessed here. A smaller model-side gap: modelTask withholds licensed text only for nodes still listed in task.requirementIds. A task planned from a licensed criterion and later relinked (PATCH task requirementIds) keeps the criterion text and point-of-focus titles, which then reach Claude through list_tasks and the task context. Trigger for the first: sign in as a member of a second organization and GET /api/corpus/file/aicpa-soc2/<path from /api/corpus>.
findings.evidence: app.ts:236 `servable` rejects only path segments equal to '.local'. app.ts:329-337 lists AICPA documents with their paths and a `present` flag for any signed-in user. app.ts:340-359 streams the file. app.ts:385-386 applies workspaceAccess only to /api/workspaces routes. corpus/README.md:73-76 and :80-84 give the licence terms and the storage location. tools.ts:239-241 iterates only `task.requirementIds`.
findings.recommendation: Add an operator setting for licensed-corpus visibility (off, single organization, all) and enforce it on the graph, node, search and corpus-file routes, serving the skeleton to tenants without entitlement. Default to the skeleton when more than one organization exists. For tasks, record on creation that the task was planned from licensed text and withhold by that marker rather than by current links.

findings.mechanism: The public trust center publishes `readiness` and `evidenceCoverage` per framework with no definition, as-of time or basis. Readiness is min(current/target, 1) over self-assessed levels that a contributor can set without evidence, and lowering targets raises it, so the roadmap principles 'readiness is computed from evidence' and 'publishes only facts that evidence backs' are not what the code computes. Evidence coverage counts any accepted item, including the automatic 'policy' evidence created for every requirement linked to an approved policy; the offline Policy Author adds sibling outcomes to that list. It also counts the items described in findings 2 and 4. A manual statusOverride of 'verified' counts toward verifiedShare in the readiness report without verifiedAt or evidence, and an override masks failing checks and expired evidence. The monitoring list de-duplicates by checkId across all connectors, so with two web-posture connectors only the most recent result per check is shown and a failing check on one site can be hidden by a pass on another. Trigger: two web-posture connectors, B failing HSTS and A passing, A run last; the public page shows HSTS pass.
findings.evidence: app.ts:684 publishes rounded readiness and evidenceCoverage. app.ts:686-688 `all.findIndex((x) => x.checkId === ch.checkId) === i`. scoring.ts:117 gives the ratio; :127 any valid evidence; :128 `status.status === "verified"`. status.ts:48-50 puts the override before the at-risk rules. visua.ts:1130-1147 creates accepted policy evidence for `next.requirementIds`. offline.ts:498-500 adds siblings. app.ts:122-131 leaves current and target ungated.
findings.recommendation: Publish what is recorded, with its basis: 'self-assessed implementation X%', 'requirements with reviewed evidence Y of N' (separating automated checks, uploads and policies), 'independently verified Z', and an as-of timestamp. Key the monitoring de-duplication on connectorId + checkId and show the target. Exclude override-only 'verified' from verifiedShare or report it separately. Classify policy evidence as design evidence and count it apart from operating evidence.

findings.mechanism: Several exports state more than the record supports. (1) OSCAL SSP: implementationStatus maps level 0 ('not implemented and not yet planned' on Visua's own scale) to 'planned'. The not-applicable branch is unreachable because only applicable controls are exported, so tailoring decisions and their rationales never appear. import-profile points at the stock NIST baseline for `categorization.overall ?? baseline`, while implemented-requirements includes PRIVACY-baseline, tailored-in and COSAiS-added controls and omits tailored-out ones with no profile modification. System status is 'operational' for any ATO regardless of `expiresAt`, and the component is always 'operational'. Every UUID is regenerated per export, so two exports of the same state cannot be diffed or referenced. (2) POA&M and the readiness report's 'Largest gaps' read stored `applicable`. Law date-scoping is applied only when scores are read, so obligations past their `until` date remain 'applicable' in storage and are exported as open items; agents and the server also still accept levels on them. Upcoming obligations are listed as today's gaps while the headline readiness excludes them. (3) csvCell does not neutralise leading = + - @, so user-controlled titles, notes and owners can become spreadsheet formulas in files sent to auditors. Trigger for (1): enable SP 800-53, export oscal-ssp.json with untouched states; every control reads implementation-status 'planned'.
findings.evidence: exports.ts:241-245 returns 'planned' for both level 1 and the fallthrough. exports.ts:258 `inScope = …filter(applicable)`; :272 the import-profile href; :293 the status state; :262, :280, :305, :311 randomUUID(). exports.ts:333 and :221 use `st.applicable`. visua.ts:432-433 applies `until` only when initializeStates runs; :815-818 applies it per score read. exports.ts:10-13 is csvCell. levels.ts:85 labels level 0 'Not implemented … not yet planned'.
findings.recommendation: Omit the status or use a distinct non-OSCAL prop for level 0 instead of asserting 'planned'. Emit tailoring as a profile (or as set-parameters and remarks) with rationales. Derive system state from the decision and its expiry. Use deterministic UUIDs (v5 over workspace id + control id). Route every export through one 'effective state as of date' function shared with scoreOf so ended and upcoming obligations are treated identically everywhere. Prefix cells that start with = + - @ with an apostrophe.

findings.mechanism: An obligation's node id is positional: `${lawCode}-${String(oi + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`, where `oi` is the obligation's index in obligations.json. Law codes are protected (CODE_OVERRIDES and a duplicate check), but any corpus refresh that inserts, removes or reorders an obligation inside a law renumbers every later obligation. Requirement states, evidence, tasks, policies and audit entries are keyed by node id, so recorded levels, 'not applicable' rationales and accepted evidence silently attach to a different statutory obligation. Nothing fails, because all ids still exist. The stable source id (`o.id`) is available and stored only as an attribute. The tests pin counts (26 / 187) and law codes, not the obligation-id-to-code assignment. Trigger: a deliberate refresh that adds an obligation as the second entry of CA-SB243; the workspace's evidence for CA-SB243-02 now sits on the new text.
findings.evidence: state-laws.ts:173-176 `for (const [oi, o] of law.obligations.entries()) { const ocode = `${code}-${String(oi + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`; … id: `${fw}:${ocode}``; :189 `obligationId: o.id`. frameworks.test.ts:249-260 checks counts and law codes only. docs/architecture.md:629 and corpus/README.md:42-43 note that laws change quickly.
findings.recommendation: Before the first corpus refresh, freeze the mapping: commit an `obligationId → code` table (or a `code` field in obligations.json), fail ingestion when a published code would change meaning, and give new obligations the next unused number. Add a test that pins the table, and a migration note for existing workspaces if codes ever must move.

findings.mechanism: The hash chain proves the sequence of audit summaries, not the facts behind claims. (1) Evidence events carry no data: the chained entry records the title and codes, not the evidence id's content digest, status, validity window or reviewer. An evidence row can be changed in storage (or through the PATCH in finding 1, which logs only 'updated') without any chained record of what changed. (2) verifyAuditTrail recomputes links from genesis to the stored head; nothing anchors the head outside the same database, so dropping the newest N events verifies clean. The code comment says 'any edit, deletion or reordering breaks the chain'. (3) Flight-recorder steps (tool calls, citations, model reasoning) are persisted outside the chain. (4) Agent execution leaves the principal context, so connector runs by agents, proposal creation and autonomy-applied changes are logged with actor 'agent:<run>' or 'autonomy (via run_…)' and no actorId. The person who started the run is only on the run record, and the admin who granted autonomy only in an earlier 'Workspace settings updated' entry that records field names. Trigger for (2): delete the last three activity rows; GET /activity/verify returns valid: true.
findings.evidence: visua.ts:1036 and :1069 call this.log without a `data` argument. visua.ts:235-242 iterates only existing events and returns the computed head. visua.ts:148-156 updates runs through txContext.exit, outside log. visua.ts:1347 `principalContext.exit(...)`. visua.ts:209 reads actorId from principalContext. visua.ts:1550 passes "autonomy" as actor. visua.ts:507 logs `{ fields: Object.keys(patch) }`.
findings.recommendation: Put a digest of the entity's canonical post-state (and of the evidence content hash) in every audit event's data. Log before and after values for links, validity and autonomy. Carry `startedBy` into agent-originated events as `onBehalfOf`. Export a signed head (seq, hash, time) on a schedule and with every auditor export so truncation is detectable. Hash each run's ordered steps into the 'finished' event.

findings.mechanism: templateFor falls back to POLICY_TEMPLATES[0], which is the AI governance policy, for any code that matches no prefix. Unmatched codes include SP 800-53 SI-1 and SI-3, SA-1 and SA-3, every RMF task (P-1, C-2, …) and every state-law obligation code. The offline Policy Author then drafts an 'Artificial Intelligence Governance and Risk Management Policy' whose statements are that control's text, with AI-committee roles, and proposes it. Once a person approves the policy it becomes accepted evidence for the control (finding 8). The composed document's mapping table is headed 'Also satisfies', which presents crosswalk mappings as satisfaction, against the product's own rule that a mapping is never evidence. Trigger: run policy-author offline with input.nodeIds = ["nist-sp-800-53-r5:SI-3"].
findings.evidence: policies.ts:213 `return best?.t ?? POLICY_TEMPLATES[0]!;` and :21-36 show the first template is 'ai-governance-policy' with matches GOVERN / MAP / MEASURE / MANAGE. The match lists at :48-198 have no 'SI', 'SA' (only SA-4, SA-8, SA-9, SA-10, SA-11, SA-15), RMF or law prefixes. policies.ts:303 `| Requirement | Framework | Also satisfies |`. offline.ts:494 uses templateFor(nodes[0]).
findings.recommendation: Return no template when nothing matches and have the agent ask which policy applies, or fall back to the Information Security Policy by id, not by array position. Add the missing family prefixes and a test asserting that every assessable SP 800-53 family and CSF category resolves to a non-AI template. Rename the column 'Related requirements (mapped, not evidence)'.

limitations: Source-only review of the packet: no tests, ingestion, agent run, connector or export was executed by this lane. Every finding is an inference from the numbered source; the lead's '214 passed / 2 skipped' was not reproduced here.

Not in the packet and therefore not reviewed: the storage layer (store, repositories, migrations), auth/http.ts and auth/service.ts, services/views.ts (workspaceSummary, nodeDetail, frameworkState, onTrustCenter), the web app, seed data, scripts/check.ts, .gitignore, the corpus manifests and the generated data files. Statements about evidence supersession, trust-center framework filtering and the manifest 'framework' value for AICPA documents assume nothing in those files changes the behaviour described.
Finding 3 assumes no background job expires, supersedes or deletes evidence; none appears in the service code provided.

Corpus content, official counts, quotation accuracy and page numbers were not checked against any source. No statement here confirms that any law, draft or standard in the corpus is current, and nothing here is legal or licensing advice; finding 7 flags a boundary for the operator to assess.
The Claude runtime's API parameters (model id, betas, fallbacks, thinking and effort fields) were not validated against a live API; no paid agent execution was performed.
Tenant isolation, CSRF, sessions, SSO, connector egress and path safety, and concurrency belong to other lanes and were touched only where they bear on evidence or licensing claims.
Documentation drift noticed but not verified: README and architecture.md cite 202 Vitest tests against the lead's 214, and 22 versus 21 Playwright tests.

Lesser observations left out of the 12 findings: ended state-law obligations stay assessable because stored applicability is date-scoped only when settings change; law status (for example 'enjoined') does not affect scope when obligations exist; SP 800-53 enhancements inherit the base control's page; linked requirements may be non-assessable group nodes or belong to disabled frameworks; the AI overview's GAI risk readiness divides by all linked outcomes including out-of-scope ones; threat level 4 'Full' is computed only over linked requirements in enabled frameworks and in scope, and the default filter counts unreviewed links.
strengths: Agents cannot reach storage. AgentHost exposes reads plus propose(), each agent has an explicit tool subset re-checked per call (claude.ts:147), inputs are zod-validated before execution, and a truncated tool input stops the run instead of executing.

One rule set for people and agents: assessableIn, linkedRequirements and checkAssessment refuse threat nodes, disabled frameworks and levels on out-of-scope requirements, both when a proposal is created and again when it is applied inside a savepoint.
Check-backed evidence is built on approval from the stored CheckResult (title, detail, requirements, observation hash), not from the proposal text, and the same check cannot be filed twice.

'Not applicable' needs a written rationale for people and proposals. userExclusion is kept apart from configuration scope and re-applied by effectiveScope on every recomputation, and re-including a requirement that configuration excludes is refused with the reason.

Licensed-text gating is centralised and tested: modelText, modelTask and passageAllowed cover requirement text, points of focus, mapped-requirement snippets, corpus quotes and text copied into tasks and the run context. Chunks are stored per corpus so AICPA data stays local, and .local folders and symlink escapes are refused by the corpus file route.

Threat catalogs are structurally separate from the crosswalk: a separate index, no assessable path in tools or service, enablement refused, every link keeping its publisher and status, weakest-link path status, and coverage weighted by publication and route so one draft citing 67 outcomes counts once.

Provenance is carried in the data model: every node has a citation, mapping sets record authority (the Visua editorial and composed sets are labeled), overlays carry NIST's own draft status and notice, and draft PDFs are excluded from page chunks while overlay chunks state their status.

Ingestion fails loudly on integrity problems: overlay entries must attach to existing nodes, law codes may not collide, dangling mapping endpoints are dropped and counted, and the tests pin official counts and require every cited document to be in a manifest.

Statutory obligations are scoped only by roles an approver records per law. Role vocabulary is validated against the law's own definitions, upcoming obligations are scored apart from today's readiness, and the trust center keeps state-law readiness private by default.

Visua-authored scales state their basis (levels.ts): each says it is a Visua convention and what it is not. The SOC 2 description view separates drafted facts from 'needs management input', and the readiness export ends with a not-an-audit-opinion statement.

The audit write path is sound: the event is written in the same transaction as the change under the workspace lock, with canonical JSON hashing and the authenticated principal id on person-initiated events.

opportunities.outcome: Next phase: Evidence foundations, delivered as one workflow. A requirement's evidence moves through collect → review → accept → supersede/expire, and every published figure (status, evidence coverage, trust center, exports) can be traced to accepted, hashed, unexpired artifacts. This closes findings 1-4 and is the precondition for every other track.
opportunities.evidence: Findings 1-4, 8 and 11. Today accepted evidence is mutable (app.ts:520-528), agent narratives are accepted on proposal approval (visua.ts:1633-1645), expired superseded items flip status (status.ts:59-60), and only two paths compute sha256. The roadmap already lists object storage, lineage and a claim-consistency agent as items 2, 4 and 7, but as separate features.
opportunities.acceptance: API and core tests on SQLite and Postgres show: (a) a contributor cannot change links or validity of accepted evidence without it returning to pending-review; (b) invalid dates are rejected; (c) agent-proposed non-check evidence lands as pending-review, is never auto-accepted, and attestation kind is refused; (d) expired + fresh evidence in one series does not yield at-risk, and a second connector run supersedes instead of duplicating; (e) every evidence record has a content hash and every evidence audit event carries it; (f) a lineage endpoint returns, for a trust-center figure or a requirement status, the evidence ids, hashes, reviewers and source checks behind it. One e2e test walks upload → review → expiry → refresh for one requirement.
